newsitem.title: USA: Samsonite shares up on restructuring plan.
newsitem.headline: Samsonite shares up on restructuring plan.

text.p: Shares of Samsonite Corp. rose strongly Friday after the world's largest luggage maker Thursday unveiled a restructuring plan that would cut 6 percent of its workforce.

The stock was up $3.25 to $37 in Nasdaq trading in late afternoon Friday. The move to layoff 450 workers and a related one-time charge of $10.7 million were announced after the close of regular trading Thursday.
In an interview Friday, Samsonite Chief Executive Officer Richard Nicolosi blamed recent company losses on a corporate approach that had become "too traditional, too conservative, too boring."
"The company operated like a conglomerate. There was no cohesive strategy," said Nicolosi, who became CEO in May.
Nicolosi declined to predict when the company would return to profitability, but added, "if we don't turn a profit by early in the next fiscal year I will be very disappointed."

With the streamlining expected to generate annual pre-tax savings of about $12.7 million, Nicolosi said Samsonite also wants to reduce its debt by $50 million by the end of the next fiscal year. Debt currently stands at $300 million, down from $356 million a year ago, he said.
